quality_guards: COSHH controls depend on the substance, form, concentration, exposure route, task, duration, workforce and effectiveness of existing controls.
COSHH evidence is substance-, process- and exposure-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
LEV performance depends on the contaminant source, hood design, airflow, process conditions, worker position, maintenance and commissioning data.
LEV evidence is process-, system- and operating-condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level inhalation-risk probability.
RPE suitability depends on the contaminant, airborne form, concentration, oxygen level, wearer, task, duration and other PPE.
RPE evidence is hazard-, wearer- and task-specific and is not an exact parcel-level respiratory-disease probability.
Skin controls depend on the substance, contact route, wet-work duration, task, glove compatibility, worker sensitivity and hygiene practices.
Skin-exposure evidence is substance-, task- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level dermatitis or cancer probability.
First-aid provision depends on workforce size, hazards, work patterns, remoteness, vulnerable people, accident history and access to emergency services.
First-aid evidence is workplace-, workforce- and hazard-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury-outcome probability.
Lone-working controls depend on the task, location, worker, communication method, supervision, travel, violence risk and emergency response.
Lone-working evidence is worker-, task- and location-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
Homeworking controls depend on the job, duration, equipment, home environment, worker needs, communication and emergency arrangements.
Homeworking evidence is worker-, task- and environment-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health or accident probability.
Temperature controls depend on indoor or outdoor conditions, work rate, radiant heat, humidity, clothing, worker vulnerability and exposure duration.
Temperature evidence is workplace-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level heat- or cold-illness probability.
Ladder suitability depends on task duration, height, surface, stability, securing method, public or vehicle interaction, load and user competence.
Ladder evidence is equipment-, task- and location-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fall probability.
Overhead-line controls depend on voltage, line position, clearance, plant dimensions, access routes, ground conditions, weather and network-owner instructions.
Overhead-line evidence is line-, activity- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level electric-shock or flashover probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
